extra.message: renderFilingBrief() builds a shell command with execSync() and interpolates `requestedFormat` directly into it. requestedFormat comes from the client-controlled `x-brief-format` header (app.matters.$matterId.brief.tsx:30), so an attacker can inject shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary OS commands.

searchAuditTrailByDateRange() uses prisma.$queryRawUnsafe with `${keyword}`, `${fromDate}` and `${toDate}` concatenated directly into the SQL string. These values originate from query parameters (app.audit._index.tsx:75), allowing SQL injection.

evaluateDamagesWorksheet() compiles attacker-controlled worksheet text with `new Function(...Object.keys(context), `return (${userFormula});`)`. The formula comes from the uploaded damages-worksheet file (app.matters.$matterId.documents.new.tsx:82-89), which even a client (low-privilege) can upload. This is arbitrary server-side code execution.

loadFilingTemplate() joins the user-supplied templateName directly onto the filing-template directory without basename/containment checks. templateName comes from the URL path (app.matters.$matterId.filing-templates.$templateName.tsx:18), so `../../` sequences can escape the directory and read arbitrary `.md` files.

archiveWorksheetSnapshot() builds a file path from the attacker-controlled worksheetLabel (the document title, from a multipart form field) without any basename/sanitization. A crafted title containing `../` lets an uploader write files outside the intended archive directory.

pullFiledExhibitCopy() fetches an arbitrary sourceUrl supplied by staff with no hostname allowlist, MIME check, or size limit (contrast with pullRegistryExhibitCopy which validates all three), then writes the retrieved bytes into the public web root (./public/exhibits) and returns a same-origin URL. This is SSRF plus an arbitrary-file-write into the public document root (enabling stored content/XSS served from the app origin).

resolveDeclaredEntities() expands SYSTEM entities declared in a feed's DOCTYPE and, for `file://` URIs, reads the referenced file directly with readFileSync. A feed fetched by syncCourtDocketFeed (fed an arbitrary URL by staff) can exfiltrate local files via external entity expansion.

syncCourtDocketFeed() (and syncFirmAnnouncementFeed()) fetch an arbitrary feedUrl with no hostname or scheme allowlist, allowing SSRF against internal services from staff/admin-driven actions (docket.feed_sync and announcements.feed_sync).

The referral-packet loader authorizes access using decodeHandoffAssertion(), which only base64-decodes the assertion and does NOT verify its HMAC signature (verifyHandoffAssertion is the function that checks the signature). An attacker can craft a self-signed assertion containing any matterId and scope 'referral_packet' to read the matter's client name/email/phone and attorney email/phone without authentication.

advanceTaskStatus() updates a task by id with no matter-scope check. The action (lines 26-44) only requires any staff role, so an attorney/paralegal can change the status of any task in the firm (including tasks on matters they cannot access) by guessing/obtaining task IDs (IDOR).

applyClientContactUpdate() spreads the entire submitted form (`Object.fromEntries(form)`) into the Prisma update data. A client can therefore submit arbitrary fields (e.g. status, accountId, conflictNotes) to modify their own client record beyond the intended reach-information fields (mass assignment).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: buildDocumentPreviewBootstrap() interpolates documentTitle and tags directly into an inline <script> string without any escaping (contrast with buildMatterOverviewBootstrap which uses jsonScriptSafe). Both values are attacker-controlled document metadata (title/tags set at upload), producing stored XSS when the document detail page renders via DocumentPreviewBootstrap (app.documents.$documentId.tsx:210).

renderPortalSummary() injects the matter description (attacker/staff-controlled) into dangerouslySetInnerHTML after only replacing `**bold**` markers, without HTML-escaping. This renders on the client portal (app.matters.$matterId.tsx:792) and permits stored XSS (contrast with renderStaffSummary which escapes first).
A hardcoded notary-vendor API secret (nlk_9f3c2a7b5d1e4408b6a2f0c9d7e5b3a1) is committed in source and used as the bearer token for notary API calls, exposing the vendor integration credential.

applySavedReportView() parses a JSON `view` query parameter and merges it into a config object via mergeConfigLayer() without stripping dangerous keys. A `__proto__`/`constructor` key recurses onto Object.prototype (applySavedReportView does not call sanitizeConfigOverrides, unlike applyDigestPreferences), enabling prototype pollution that can be amplified by the bundled Handlebars dependency.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

extra.message: buildDirectoryFilter() merges a JSON-parsed `view` query parameter wholesale into the Prisma where clause (`{ ...base, ...savedCriteria }`). Unlike the matter-list equivalent which whitelists fields, this lets a caller inject arbitrary Prisma filter operators/relations into the query.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: streamWorksheetArchive() returns `downloadName: worksheetLabel + '.txt'` from unsanitized user input, which app.matters.$matterId.edit.tsx places into the Content-Disposition header. A label containing CRLF sequences enables HTTP response-header/splitting (the safeDownloadName helper exists in storage.server but is not used here).

resolveMatterIntakeDestination() returns the raw `x-continue-url` header as the redirect target after creating a matter, without validating it is same-origin (contrast with resolveClientIntakeDestination in app.clients.new.tsx which checks origin). This is an open redirect.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: DRAFT_KEY falls back to a hardcoded all-zero 64-hex key when INTAKE_DRAFT_KEY is unset, meaning the intake/client resume tokens are encrypted with a predictable key. Additionally packIntakeResumeToken uses AES-256-CBC without authentication, allowing ciphertext tampering.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: provisionCoCounselPassword() hashes passwords with a default bcrypt work factor of 4 (weak), and the work factor itself is taken directly from an admin-supplied CSV field, which can also be set extremely high to cause a denial of service.

timedWidgetCorsHeaders() reflects the caller's Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests to the timed docket-status endpoint (contrast with standingWidgetCorsHeaders which uses an allowlist).

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The client-detail loader reflects the request Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true unconditionally. Combined with the session cookie configured as sameSite:none (auth.server.ts:16), a malicious site can read a logged-in staff member's client JSON cross-origin.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
